svg.title: DuckDB never materialised the rows
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing a star schema with a narrow ten-million-row fact table at the centre and four small dimension tables around it; a slowly-changing dimension drawn as three stacked versions of one merchant row carrying valid-from, valid-to and is-current, with an as-of query landing on the middle row; a bar chart of one group-by over ten million rows where DuckDB takes 0.117 seconds and 96 megabytes against pandas at 1.510 seconds and 878 megabytes, with polars in between; and two directory trees where daily partitions are marked good and two hundred and fifty thousand per-user directories are crossed out in red.
svg.text: narrow and long in the middle, wide and short around it
the fact table never changes shape. The dimensions carry the
the fact rows never move. The DIMENSION
remembers. That is the only way "revenue by
merchant tier, last March" can ever be right.
one group-by over 10,000,000 rows, same parquet file
pandas materialised 10 million rows to answer
a question about four. DuckDB never did - it
streams and it knows the file's statistics.
